criterion: TRUE on the date of the first FDA approval letter in Drugs@FDA for a drug product whose active ingredient is psilocybin, LSD (lysergide, any salt) or MDMA (midomafetamine, any salt), for any indication and from any sponsor. A complete response letter, a positive advisory vote or a filing acceptance is not an approval. FALSE at the deadline when no approval letter for such a product is dated in Drugs@FDA by then. Resolution source: Drugs@FDA.

asset: Psilocybin, LSD and MDMA drug products: retail-pharmacy dispensing under the FDA-approved labeling or REMS
entity: US Food and Drug Administration
title: Psilocybin, LSD or MDMA drug product approved with retail-pharmacy dispensing
proposition: The FDA approves a psilocybin, LSD or MDMA drug product whose approved labeling or REMS permits a retail pharmacy to dispense it to the patient for use outside a healthcare setting.
criterion: Resolved on Drugs@FDA (approval letters and approved labeling) read with the FDA REMS database (REMS@FDA). For each drug product whose active ingredient is psilocybin, LSD (lysergide, any salt) or MDMA (midomafetamine, any salt) that the FDA approves between the statement date and the deadline, check the approved labeling and any REMS in force on the approval date. TRUE on the approval date of the first such product whose labeling or REMS permits a retail or community pharmacy to dispense it to the patient or caregiver for use outside a healthcare setting. FALSE at the deadline if at least one such product has been approved and every such approval restricts dispensing to certified healthcare settings or requires administration under healthcare-provider supervision in a healthcare setting. If no such product is approved in the window, the condition is unmet and the item is void.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA (approval letters and labeling) with the FDA REMS database (REMS@FDA)

readings: 'Go through a retail pharmacy' reads as the FDA-approved labeling or REMS permitting a retail or community pharmacy to dispense the product to the patient for use outside a healthcare setting.

A product restricted to certified healthcare settings, or whose label requires administration under healthcare-provider supervision in a healthcare setting (the Spravato model the author uses as the reference), does not go through a retail pharmacy.

'Them' and 'these drugs' = drug products whose active ingredient is psilocybin, LSD (lysergide) or MDMA (midomafetamine), in any salt or formulation the sponsor names as such. 'None of them' denies the disjunction, so one event covers all three ('A or B' is one event).

Denial: the forecaster asserts that the proposition is false. The claim presupposes at least one approval; if none occurs in the window, the condition is unmet and the item is void rather than scored as a correct denial.

asset: Novel psychedelic drug products: FDA labeling and REMS with no required in-clinic monitoring during or after dosing
entity: US Food and Drug Administration
title: FDA approves a psychedelic drug product with no required post-dose monitoring
proposition: The FDA approves a novel psychedelic drug product whose labeling and REMS omit any requirement for in-clinic monitoring of the patient during and after dosing.
criterion: Resolved on Drugs@FDA (approval letters and labeling) read with REMS@FDA. A novel psychedelic drug product is the first FDA-approved product with a psychedelic or entactogen active ingredient (the class the forecaster illustrates with psilocybin, LSD and MDMA); ketamine and esketamine products and new formulations of approved drugs do not count. TRUE on the approval date of the first such product, approved after the statement date, whose labeling and REMS require no monitoring of the patient by a healthcare provider during or after dosing (no observation period, no certified-setting dosing requirement). FALSE at the deadline if at least one such product has been approved and every one requires in-clinic monitoring during or after dosing. If none is approved in the window, the condition is unmet and the item is void.

asset: Novel psychedelic drug products: FDA labeling or REMS that requires video recording of dosing sessions
entity: US Food and Drug Administration
title: Psychedelic drug product labeling or REMS requires video recording of dosing sessions
proposition: The FDA approves a novel psychedelic drug product whose labeling or REMS requires video recording (auditable video) of dosing sessions.
criterion: Resolved on Drugs@FDA (approval letters and labeling) read with REMS@FDA. A novel psychedelic drug product is the first FDA-approved product with a psychedelic or entactogen active ingredient (the class the forecaster illustrates with psilocybin, LSD and MDMA); ketamine and esketamine do not count. TRUE on the approval date of the first such product, approved after the statement date, whose labeling or REMS (including elements to assure safe use) requires video recording of dosing sessions, or a video record of each session kept or available for audit. Observation without recording, a non-binding recommendation, or a sponsor's voluntary program outside the labeling or REMS does not count. FALSE at the deadline if at least one such product has been approved and none carries such a requirement. If none is approved in the window, the condition is unmet and the item is void.
